about: The Alma Redemptoris Mater is the final Marian antiphon for the season from Advent through the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary. The faithful ask Mary, Mother of the Redeemer, to help the falling people and have mercy on sinners.

seg.tr: Loving Mother of the Redeemer, who remain the open gate of heaven,

fn.w001: The vocative adjective addresses Mary as nurturing, gracious and venerable Mother.
fn.w002: The genitive depends on “Mater” and names Christ the Redeemer.
fn.w003: The vocative opens the direct address to Mary.
fn.w004: The relative refers to Mary and is the subject of “manes”.
fn.w005: It describes the gate as accessible and passable.
fn.w007: A predicate nominative with “manes”: Mary remains the gate of heaven.
fn.w008: The second person continues the direct address. The verb links the predicate nouns “porta” and “stella”.

seg.tr: and star of the sea, help the people who are falling,

fn.w010: The second predicate nominative with “manes”, coordinated with “porta”.
fn.w012: The antiphon's first imperative. It governs the dative “pópulo” in the next segment.
fn.w013: The dative participle agrees with “pópulo” across the segment boundary.

fn.w014: The fronted infinitive complements “curat”: the people strive to rise.
fn.w015: Its masculine singular form resumes the collective “pópulo”.
fn.w016: Together with “súrgere”, it expresses concern, desire and effort to rise.
fn.w017: The dative governed by “succúrre”. The same people are falling and strive to rise.

seg.tr: you who, while nature marvelled, gave birth to your holy Creator,

fn.w018: The emphatic nominative again identifies Mary as addressee and mother.
fn.w019: The relative is the subject of “genuísti” and refers to Mary.
fn.w020: The perfect names the completed birth. Its object is “Genitórem”.
fn.w021: The subject of the ablative absolute formed with “miránte”.
fn.w022: The deponent participle has active meaning. With “natúra” it forms an ablative absolute.
fn.w023: The relation to Mary sharpens the paradox: she bore her own Creator.
fn.w025: The accusative object of “genuísti”. The title names Christ as the one who brought Mary into being.

fn.w026: The vocative describes the same addressee as Virgin.
fn.w027: The adverb relates virginity to the time before the birth.
fn.w029: The adverb affirms virginity also after the birth.

seg.tr: receiving that Ave from Gabriel's mouth, have mercy on sinners.

fn.w031: The preposition with the ablative identifies the source of the received greeting.
fn.w032: The ablative governed by “ab” literally means “from the mouth”. The genitive “Gabriélis” names the angel who spoke.
fn.w033: The participle refers to Mary and supplies the circumstance of the final petition.
fn.w034: The neuter points to the quoted word “Ave” as a complete salutation.
fn.w035: The greeting's imperative is quoted here and, as a whole quotation, serves as the object of “sumens”.
fn.w036: The genitive plural is the complement governed by “miserére”.
fn.w037: The second imperative, deponent in form, closes the antiphon with a direct petition to Mary.
